records.text: An anonymous police officer wrote that the Axon Body 4 camera battery lasts approximately 14 hours and cameras must be docked after every shift.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep mLvJqdxS-FY)

appearances.snippet: The camera battery lasts approximately 14 hours. At the end of every shift, we have to dock our cameras all on a detachment shared dock.

verification.notes: The episode records Candace Owens reading an anonymous message that states an approximately 14-hour battery life and end-of-shift docking. Current Axon documentation independently confirms a full-shift battery and that docking charges the camera and uploads evidence, but it does not substantiate an exact universal 14-hour runtime or a universal every-shift policy. The anonymous authorship cannot be independently authenticated.

sources.title: Axon Body 4 care and maintenance
sources.relevance: Official Axon guidance confirms dock charging and simultaneous evidence upload, but not the full anonymous claim.

records.text: An anonymous police officer wrote that Axon's system records why a video stops or a device turns off and that police can review that information.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep mLvJqdxS-FY)

appearances.snippet: The Axon body force system also logs and records the specific reason a video stops or device turns off. All of this information can be seen on the Axon site that the police have access to and can review.

verification.notes: The episode records the anonymous message asserting that Axon logs the specific reason a recording stops or a device powers off and that police can review it. Current Axon guidance confirms device audit-trail entries for some camera state changes, including entering and leaving sleep mode, but the accessible documentation did not confirm the broader claim that every stop or shutdown has a specific recorded reason. Anonymous authorship also cannot be authenticated.
